teaching.hint: How could reflection paths be compared with straight travel across repeated copies of the room?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Unfolding reflections turns the ray into a straight line through tiled squares; the first corner hit is determined by the reduced ratio of p and q.
solution_outline.approach: Reduce p and q by their gcd. The number of horizontal and vertical room crossings to the first lattice corner are the reduced p and q; their parities identify east/west and top/bottom.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The unfolded ray has slope q/p. The first positive room-grid intersection uses horizontal count p/g and vertical count q/g, with g=gcd(p,q).
solution_outline.correctness: Unfolding preserves the reflected route. Coprime reduced counts identify the first corner; odd/even crossing parity maps the tiled corner back to a room corner. Both counts cannot be even, so the unlabeled source is not the first receptor.
solution_outline.complexity: O(log min(p,q)) time for gcd and O(1) space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Testing parity before dividing by gcd can classify an even/even input incorrectly.

common_wrong_turns: Assume all reflections land on the east wall
Use unreduced p and q for parity
source_fidelity_notes: Restated receptor positions and the ray’s initial east-wall height in text because the source relies on an image.
